transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're looking at a proposed eighth-grade makerspace program for the spring semester involving soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter. The draft calls for 24 students with one STEM teacher supervising, meeting twice weekly. Before I make a final authorization decision, I'd like to gather input from each of you on the implementation details. Let's start with you, STEM teacher — could you walk us through how you're planning to run this program, particularly around supervision and safety?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, before I walk through the plan, I need to flag an important safety finding. I completed a room-safety review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers — 24 students with one supervisor — so those will need to be revised before this program can be authorized.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important health-related finding from my review of the participating students' health records. I found that one student has a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I also want to note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file, so we'll need to make sure that happens.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important technology finding. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program still contains the cloud-storage instruction, so that will need to be revised before authorization.
